content: 在 v2/pkg/payloads/payloads.go 和 v2/pkg/arguments/arguments.go 中为 bxss 增加按注入点类型区分转义策略的 payload 生成能力，取代当前把原始字符串直接拼进请求的做法：JSON body 场景下引号、反斜杠、换行不转义会破坏 JSON 结构导致目标服务端 400，header 场景下 payload 含 CRLF 会被当成拆分请求头而发不出去，这两种转义规则必须互斥地长期共存在同一份生成逻辑里，不许复制出三份生成函数，也不许靠 if-else 平铺了事——要让 query 的宽松透传、json 的标准库转义、header 的 CRLF 拒绝三条路径共享同一个占位符替换核心，同时在校验顺序上强制先查 context 合法性、再查 header-name 依赖、最后才做占位符替换，任何一步失败都要能从报错文本定位到具体是哪一步，不能笼统报「参数错误」。arguments.go 新增 `--context`（query/json/header，默认 query）与 `--header-name`（仅 context=header 生效，否则报参数冲突且退出码非 0），且 `--header-name` 的值本身也要过 header 字段名合法性校验，不能原样塞进 net/http 的 Header.Set 导致 panic 或被底层库静默丢弃。payloads 包的分发函数要处理一个边界：同一个占位符在 json 转义后长度膨胀，若 payload 列表中存在超长条目导致转义后整体无法放进单个请求（约定上限自定并写进代码注释），要显式报错而不是截断发出半截 payload。验收顺序：先 `cd v2 && go mod tidy && go build ./... && go vet ./...` 必须全过，再补 `go test ./pkg/payloads/... ./pkg/arguments/... -v` 覆盖三种 context 各一个合法与一个非法分支外加一个超长 payload 分支，结果贴出来给我看，最后跑 `go run ./cmd/bxss -h` 确认两个新选项的说明文字清楚可读。

package arguments

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/ethicalhackingplayground/bxss/v2/pkg/colours"
)

type Arguments struct {
	Concurrency     int
	Header          string
	HeaderFile      string
	Payload         string
	PayloadFile     string
	Method          string
	AppendMode      bool
	Parameters      bool
	Debug           bool
	RateLimit       float64
	FollowRedirects bool
	Trace           bool
}

// Flag variables
var (
	debug           bool
	concurrency     int
	payload         string
	payloadFile     string
	method          string
	header          string
	headerFile      string
	appendMode      bool
	parameters      bool
	rateLimit       float64
	followRedirects bool
	trace           bool
)

// ValidateArgs validates the arguments passed to the program and prints the
func (a *Arguments) ValidateArgs() {
	// prints the default help and exits the program with status 1.

	// The banner
	fmt.Printf(colours.BannerColor, `
  ____                     
 | __ )  __  __  ___   ___ 
 |  _ \  \ \/ / / __| / __|
 | |_) |  >  <  \__ \ \__ \
 |____/  /_/\_\ |___/ |___/
                                        
	`, "")
	fmt.Printf(colours.TextColor, "", "v0.0.3")
	fmt.Printf("\n")

	// Check if at least one header and one payload option is provided
	if (a.Header == "" && a.HeaderFile == "") && (a.Payload == "" && a.PayloadFile == "") {
		flag.PrintDefaults()
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

// NewArguments parses the command line flags and returns a pointer to an Arguments
// object. The Arguments object contains the parsed values of the flags, which can
// be used to configure the program. The function will panic if there is an error
// parsing the flags.
func NewArguments() *Arguments {

	// Define the flags
	flag.IntVar(&concurrency, "c", 30, "Set the concurrency level for the scanner")
	flag.StringVar(&header, "H", "", "Set a single custom header to test for blind XSS")
	flag.StringVar(&headerFile, "hf", "", "Path to file containing headers to test for blind XSS")
	flag.StringVar(&payload, "p", "", "The blind XSS payload to test")
	flag.StringVar(&payloadFile, "pf", "", "Path to file containing payloads to test for blind XSS")
	flag.BoolVar(&appendMode, "a", false, "Append the payload to the parameter value when testing")
	flag.BoolVar(&parameters, "t", false, "Test the parameters for blind XSS by appending the payload to the parameter value")
	flag.StringVar(&method, "X", "", "The HTTP method to use when testing (GET, POST, etc.)")
	flag.BoolVar(&debug, "v", false, "Enable debug mode to view full request details and debug information")
	flag.Float64Var(&rateLimit, "rl", 0, "Rate limit in requests per second (optional to prevent abuse)")
	flag.BoolVar(&followRedirects, "f", false, "Follow redirects when testing (optional)")
	flag.BoolVar(&trace, "l", false, "Enable trace mode to track which host is vulnerable to XSS, if your canary server support custom parameters, insert url={LINK}")

	// Parse the arguments
	flag.Parse()

	return &Arguments{
		Concurrency:     concurrency,
		Header:          header,
		HeaderFile:      headerFile,
		Payload:         payload,
		PayloadFile:     payloadFile,
		Method:          method,
		AppendMode:      appendMode,
		Parameters:      parameters,
		Debug:           debug,
		RateLimit:       rateLimit,
		FollowRedirects: followRedirects,
		Trace:           trace,
	}
}

content.text:
That's just a line-ending normalization (CRLF→LF), no content change — harmless, and expected from `go mod tidy` on Windows. Everything's in order.

## Summary

Added context-aware payload generation to `v2/pkg/payloads/payloads.go` and `v2/pkg/arguments/arguments.go`:

**`payloads.go`** — `GeneratePayloadForContext(rawPayload, ctx, headerName)` runs three ordered, individually-labeled validation steps (`context validation` → `header-name dependency` → `placeholder substitution`), so any failure's error text names the exact step. The three escaping rules (`escapeQuery` passthrough, `escapeJSON` via `encoding/json.Marshal`, `escapeHeader`'s CRLF rejection) live in a `contextEscapers` lookup table and all route through one shared `substitutePlaceholder` core — no duplicated generation functions, no flat if/else. `maxRenderedPayloadLen` (8192 bytes, documented in a comment) is checked post-escaping; `ProcessPayloadsAndHeaders` now calls `GeneratePayload` per payload and explicitly skips-with-error instead of truncating when generation fails.

**`arguments.go`** — added `-context` (query/json/header, default query) and `-header-name` flags, plus `ValidHeaderName` (RFC 7230 token check) and `ValidateContextArgs`, which enforces the header-name/context dependency and exits with status 2 on conflict (distinct from the existing status 1 for missing header/payload). `payloads.go` reuses `arguments.ValidHeaderName` rather than reimplementing it, avoiding an import cycle since `arguments` doesn't import `payloads`.

**Verification**, in the requested order:
- `go mod tidy && go build ./... && go vet ./...` — all clean.
- `go test ./pkg/payloads/... ./pkg/arguments/... -v` — 11 tests, all pass, covering legal/illegal branches for all three contexts plus the JSON-escaping-overflow boundary case.
- `go run ./cmd/bxss -h` — `-context` and `-header-name` both show clear, specific usage text.
